transcript.content: Hello. What brings you to the clinic today?

My team keeps telling me my behavior and decisions don’t make sense anymore, and I feel like I can’t control what I’m doing at work. My spouse and our HR director actually urged me to come in because things have gotten so difficult for me to manage lately.
Do these difficulties with your behavior and decisions come in distinct phases where you also feel unusually energetic or need very little sleep, or has this been a steady, gradual change over time?

It has been a steady, gradual slide over the last two and a half years, rather than coming in high-energy phases. This overall decline in my functioning and motivation started around the time of a major company merger and has just progressively gotten worse. I haven't had any periods where I felt unusually energetic or didn't need sleep.
Have you ever experienced a head injury, stroke, or been diagnosed with any other brain or neurological condition?
No, I have never had a head injury or a stroke. To my knowledge, I don't have any diagnosed brain or neurological conditions either.
Have you or your family noticed any new difficulties with your memory, planning daily tasks, or finding the right words when you speak?

Yes, I've had severe difficulties with planning and memory, like losing track of strategic documents, missing key calls, and struggling with basic executive tasks. My spouse and our board have definitely noticed this chaotic disorganization and erratic decision-making. I haven't really had trouble finding the right words when I speak, but the planning issues have been overwhelming.
Have your family or colleagues noticed you saying or doing socially inappropriate things, or showing a lack of empathy and concern for others' feelings?

Yes, they've noticed me snapping at people or laughing at completely inappropriate times at work, which I can't explain. I've also been ignoring calls and pulling away from everyone because I feel completely flat and detached, like the part of me that cares about anything has shut off. It really scares me because I don't understand why I'm acting this way or why I can't just behave normally.
Have you or your family noticed any new, repetitive habits or routines, or perhaps a sudden change in your eating habits, like craving sweets much more than usual?
No, I haven't noticed any changes in my eating habits or any cravings for sweets. I also haven't developed any new repetitive routines or habits that I'm aware of.

Did these changes in your behavior and personality, such as the snapping or feeling detached, start before you noticed the difficulties with your memory and planning, or did they all begin around the same time?

The difficulties with planning, organizing, and feeling detached actually started first, about two and a half years ago during a major company merger. The more erratic behaviors, like snapping at people or staring at walls, started much more recently, about three months ago.

While you struggle with planning and organizing, do you find that you can still easily remember recent conversations, daily events, and personal information, or has your memory for those specific things also declined significantly?

I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. While I don't think I've forgotten major personal details, my mind feels too scattered and disorganized lately to really keep track of how well I'm remembering specific daily events or conversations.
Have you had any new difficulties with finding your way around familiar places, judging distances while driving, or recognizing everyday objects and faces?
No, I haven't experienced those specific issues at all. I don't have any trouble getting lost in familiar places, driving, or recognizing everyday objects and faces.
Have you or your family noticed any physical changes, such as stiffness in your muscles, tremors, or changes in your balance and walking?
No, I haven't noticed any physical changes like that at all. I don't have any muscle stiffness, tremors, or issues with my balance and walking.
Aside from feeling flat and detached, have you been experiencing a persistently low, sad, or hopeless mood, or strong feelings of worthlessness and guilt?
I don't really feel a deep sadness, hopelessness, or guilt. Rather, I just feel completely empty, flat, and lacking any drive or emotion, as if my feelings have been shut off entirely.
Could you tell me how old you are, and whether anyone in your family has ever experienced similar personality changes or early-onset dementia?
I am 43 years old. To my knowledge, no one in my family has ever experienced similar personality changes or any kind of dementia.
Have you had any brain imaging, such as an MRI or CT scan, since these difficulties began, and if so, what did the results show?
No, I haven't had any brain imaging, such as an MRI or CT scan, since these difficulties began. We haven't done any tests like that yet.
Are you still able to manage your personal daily activities—such as handling your finances, taking medications, and grooming—completely on your own, or do you now require assistance with them?

I'm really struggling to manage my daily activities on my own right now. I've been neglecting basic things like showering because I just don't have the energy or motivation to do it. My spouse has had to step in and help keep me on track with my basic routines because I've become so detached from them.
Have you or your family noticed any changes in your speech, such as using fewer words, repeating certain phrases, or struggling to understand the meaning of words that used to be familiar?

I haven't really noticed those specific changes in my speech patterns, like repeating phrases or forgetting word meanings. However, I have generally been much quieter lately and avoiding conversations altogether.
Have you or your family noticed any new impulsive behaviors, such as making reckless financial decisions, sudden large purchases, or taking unusual risks that you wouldn't have taken in the past?
No, I haven't experienced any of those behaviors. I haven't made any reckless financial decisions, sudden large purchases, or taken any unusual risks.
Have your spouse or close family members noticed that you seem less warm, caring, or responsive to their emotional needs and feelings than you used to be?

Yes, my spouse has definitely noticed a change in how I react. I feel completely flat and blank inside, like the part of me that used to care about people has just shut off. Because of that, I've been pulling away from my spouse and friends, and I find it really hard to show warmth or respond to them emotionally anymore.
Have your family or colleagues noticed you acting childishly, or laughing at things that others don't find funny, in a way that seems completely out of character for you?

Yes, that is exactly what has been happening, and it is deeply embarrassing for me. I've found myself laughing or snapping at people at completely wrong moments at work, or just staring at walls and pacing the hallways. My colleagues are very alarmed by it, and I honestly can't explain to anyone why I am behaving that way.
Have you noticed any new physical weakness in your arms or legs, muscle twitching, or difficulty swallowing food or liquids?
No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I don't have any physical weakness in my arms or legs, muscle twitching, or any difficulty swallowing food or liquids.
Have you or your family noticed any sudden, unusual changes in your personal beliefs, religious views, or hobbies, such as taking up intense new interests that are completely unlike your past self?

No, I haven't experienced any sudden changes in my beliefs or taken up any new interests. Instead, I have actually lost interest in the hobbies I used to love, like my art projects and going to yoga. It feels like I just don't have the drive or care for those things anymore.

F03 remains as a non-specific dementia category. No further questioning is required to establish this differential.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient is a 43-year-old presenting with a 2.5-year history of progressive cognitive and behavioral decline, highly characteristic of early-onset behavioral variant Frontotemporal Dementia (bvFTD / Pick's disease, ICD-10: F02.0). Key diagnostic features include prominent executive dysfunction (disorganization, planning deficits), marked apathy and loss of empathy (feeling flat, detached, withdrawing from family and hobbies), and behavioral disinhibition (inappropriate laughing, snapping at colleagues). The preservation of visuospatial skills, absence of primary amnestic deficits early on, and early age of onset strongly point to F02.0 over unspecified dementia (F03). Significant functional impairment is present, as the patient requires assistance with basic activities of daily living.
